cards.text: Jesus is on His way to Jerusalem, passing between Samaria and Galilee. That's a LONG walk, friend. The longest trip I ever took was from the counter to the back of a junk drawer, and I still needed a nap.
He walks into one of the villages, and ten lepers come to meet Him. Under the law, a person with leprosy had to live alone, outside the camp (Leviticus 13:46).

cards.question: The ten lepers walk right up to Jesus to meet Him.
The ten lepers stand at a distance. How do they get Jesus' attention?

answers.text: They raise their voices and shout
They send a friend to bring Him
They wave until He comes over

cards.question: The ten lepers call out to Jesus. What do they ask Him for?

cards.text: "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!" Ten men yelling one name from a distance, like trying to find your friend across a packed parking lot. And Jesus sees them.

cards.question: When Jesus sees the ten lepers, what does He tell them to do?

answers.text: Go show yourselves to the priests
Go wash seven times in the Jordan
Come close and touch My cloak

cards.text: Under the law, a leper was brought to the priest on the day of his cleansing (Leviticus 14:2). And Jesus sends them off while they're STILL lepers, like heading to the bank with a check that hasn't even come in the mail!

cards.question: The ten lepers head off toward the priests. When are they cleansed?
One of the ten sees that he's healed. What does he do?

answers.text: He hurries on to the priests
He goes home to his family

cards.question: The healed man comes back praising God quietly, under his breath.

cards.text: He comes back praising God in a LOUD voice, the kind Mags would be proud of. I bet this man does NOT care who's watching.

cards.question: The healed man reaches Jesus. What does he do?

answers.text: Asks Jesus to heal his family
Begs to go along with Jesus

cards.text: Face to the ground, thanking Jesus. Then Luke adds one more detail about who this man is.

cards.question: Jesus is passing between Samaria and Galilee. Who is the healed man who came back?
Jesus asks where the other ___ are, since all ___ were cleansed.
Jesus asks if no one was found to return and give ___ to God except this foreigner.

cards.text: Ten men healed, ONE thank-you, and I'm just a stamper with a mustache, but I've gotten more thank-yous than that for one batch of sugar cookies. Then Jesus tells the man, "Rise and go…"

cards.question: Jesus tells the Samaritan to rise and go. What does Jesus say has made him well?

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin: 8 of the 12 choice cards are multiple choice, with only 2 true or false and 2 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This card mostly recaps Luke 17:13, which cards 4 and 5 just asked about: the shouting from a distance and the cry for mercy. Its only new beat is 'And Jesus sees them.'
This card retells that he comes back praising God in a loud voice, which card 10 (he comes back) and card 11 (not quietly) just asked about. It adds nothing new from the passage, only a reaction.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: 'Face to the ground' recaps Luke 17:16, which card 13 just asked about. Only 'thanking Jesus' and the lead-in to the Samaritan detail are new.
The card calls them 'Ten men.' The text calls them ten lepers (Luke 17:12) and never says all ten were men.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card says 'Ten men healed.' The text calls them lepers and says 'all ten' were cleansed (Luke 17:17). It never says all ten were men.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke laughs at the nine who didn't return instead of at Papa Dorin himself. It also puts the stamper ahead of Jesus in thank-yous received, which isn't humble.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: The joke's logic doesn't click. 'I'm just a stamper with a mustache, but I've gotten more thank-yous' sets up a contrast that being a stamper doesn't explain, so a stranger would say 'huh?'

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: 'A Pharisee' isn't the same kind of thing as the other answers. 'A Samaritan' and 'A Galilean' say where someone is from, but 'A Pharisee' is a religious party. 'Who is the healed man' is also vague. Ask where he's from and use a people group like 'A Judean' as the third answer.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
